$comment: What a person is allowed to read on their way into this product.
Every rule here failed on a shipped file at some point: an onboarding
screen that said four of twelve capabilities were ready on every machine
in the world, a setup guide naming a package nobody had published, a
screenshot manifest describing a connected engine because the string was
a constant, an install command with a maintainer's drive letter in it.
The scan is deliberately narrow. A repository-wide sweep for these words
is almost all noise -- `placeholder` is a DOM attribute, `not implemented`
is usually an honest capability disclosure, `temporary` is a directory --
and a gate that cries wolf gets an allowlist bolted on until it means
nothing. So the surfaces are listed by name, and so is every exemption.
for the text, JSON, package descriptions and npm tarballs, and
`tests/test_release_surface.py` for the CLI help and the wheel and sdist.
One table, so a rule cannot be relaxed on one side only.
